pass_summary: The feature is implemented as planned. worker-access.ts is pure and git-free, the quoting is sound, and denies only cover directories outside the worktree. worker_access is gated on startPath === 'prewarmed', the server injects workerDirs, and the prose is symmetric across the 4 target files. The main gap is that orca_start never reports why the inline config was skipped (invalid OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT, Windows, none) or which directories were dropped for glob characters, although the plan requires it. There are also a few robustness edges in the merge and in withAccess.

issues.title: orca_start does not surface the skip reason or skippedDirs
issues.description: The plan's In Scope says 'Reporting: orca_start reports worker_access … or the reason it was skipped', and that a glob-named directory 'is skipped and reported'. opencodeLaunch returns `skipped` and `skippedDirs` (src/orca/worker-access.ts:56-59), but src/orca/mcp-tools-start.ts only reads `launch?.access` in withAccess (:316-342). So an invalid user OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT, win32, or a dropped glob directory leaves no visible trace, and the worker then silently prompts again. That is the symptom this feature removes.
issues.suggested_fix: In mcp-tools-start.ts, when start_path is 'prewarmed' and the agent is opencode, add `worker_access: { skipped: launch.skipped }` (or `worker_access_skipped`) plus `skipped_dirs` to the JSON and a text line when `launch.skipped`/`launch.skippedDirs` is set. Add a test with OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT='not json' that asserts the reason appears.

issues.title: Merge drops a non-object agent-level `permission` (and a top-level string `permission`)
issues.description: In src/orca/worker-access.ts:143-154, `permission` is copied only when `isObject(config.permission)`, and each agent's `a.permission` only when it is an object. If the user's OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT uses a shorthand string action (e.g. `"permission": "allow"` or `agent.build.permission: "ask"`, if OpenCode accepts that form), it is replaced by `{}` plus denies, and the user's setting is lost. That is the 'user settings lost' risk the plan mitigates with a deep merge. Only a string `permission.edit` is wrapped (addRules). There is no test for existing agent-level permissions.
issues.suggested_fix: Apply the same string→`{"*": value}` wrapping at the `permission` level, both top-level and per agent, before adding rules (or skip with a reason when the shape is unknown). Add a test that merges an existing `agent.build.permission.edit` object and string.

issues.title: withAccess uses a string replacement that interprets `$` patterns
issues.description: src/orca/mcp-tools-start.ts:338-341 calls `.replace("- Next:", `…${a.dirs.join(", ")}…`)`. A string replacement expands `$&`, `$'` and `` $` ``, so a directory path containing `$'` or `$&` (allowed by the extra-dirs list) would corrupt the text line. The JSON half already uses a function replacer. The rewrite also silently does nothing if formatStart ever stops emitting a ```json fence or '- Next:', and the text line looks untested (the tests assert only `r.data.worker_access`).
issues.suggested_fix: Use a function replacer: `.replace("- Next:", () => `- The worker can read … \n- Next:`)`. Better still, add `worker_access` inside formatStart's data object before rendering instead of re-parsing the fenced JSON. Add an assertion on the text line.

issues.title: 'Inside the worktree' test uses startsWith('..') on the relative path
issues.description: src/orca/worker-access.ts:121 treats any `rel` starting with '..' as outside the worktree. A directory inside the worktree whose name starts with two dots (e.g. `<wt>/..cache`) yields rel '..cache', so the worker would get a `..cache/*` deny on its own files. That is the 'deny covers own worktree' risk, in an unlikely form.
issues.suggested_fix: Use `rel === ".." || rel.startsWith(".." + sep)` (and `isAbsolute(rel)` for other roots) to decide 'outside'. Add a unit test with a `..name` subdirectory.

issues.title: Glob check runs on the raw path, not the realpath used in the patterns
issues.description: GLOB.test(d) (worker-access.ts:114) checks the input. The emitted patterns use `abs = resolve(real(d))` and `rel`, so a symlink whose target contains `*?[]{}` produces unescaped glob patterns, which could widen the allow/deny.
issues.suggested_fix: Test GLOB against `abs` (and the resolved worktree for `rel`) after realpath, and report those directories in skippedDirs.
